runner.tool_cache_note: host-local and gitignored; only its HASHES are tracked

documented_json_interface.input_format: JSON array of program strings (--fmt programs-list, the default)

input_parity.finding: The two files DIFFER BY BYTES but carry the same 250 programs in the same order -- the difference is formatting only. So the Python reproduction's input is content-identical to what the core at the bindings' pinned revision ships, and a Rust-vs-Python comparison is like-for-like on content. It is NOT like-for-like on bytes, and a comparison must fix ONE input file rather than let each route use its own in-tree copy, or the difference between routes would include a dataset difference.

checks.claim: source is at the revision the BINDINGS pin, not at main's head
the MIT grant is explicit in the acquired copy: LICENSE file AND Cargo.toml
the grant's one condition is identified, so redistribution terms are known
the JSON interface is DOCUMENTED for exactly this use, not improvised
the input is content-identical to the one the Python reproduction used
a Rust toolchain exists on this host

unrun_or_blocked: THE BUILD. cargo, rustc and rustup are all absent from this host -- the same measured toolchain gap that blocks DreamCoder (BLK-DC-3). Everything else this route needs is verified above. Installing a Rust toolchain is a host change and is the operator's decision, not this seat's.
why: the Python bindings' licence is unresolved for the distributed package; the Rust core's MIT grant is explicit at the pinned revision, so this asks whether the same capability is reachable through the core's documented JSON interface instead

budget_profile.purpose: run a first-useful-check or a reproduction fixture against ALREADY acquired bytes.
budget_profile.network: FORBIDDEN -- enforced by the check harness, which asserts no acquisition step runs under this profile
budget_profile.rationale: Scientific execution uses already-available inputs and dependencies. A check that needs the network is an acquisition step wearing a check's name.
budget_profile.name: offline_check

resource_receipt.network_policy: FORBIDDEN -- enforced by the check harness, which asserts no acquisition step runs under this profile
resource_receipt.rss_enforcement: NOT ENFORCED -- no job object / cgroup cap. peak_rss_bytes_os_counter is the OS peak-working-set counter for this process and IS reliable; rss_ceiling_exceeded_during_sampling is sampled and can miss a spike. Neither stops a step.
resource_receipt.rss_excludes_children: This is THIS process only. pip, git and venv run as children and their RSS is NOT included.

decision_point.question: install a Rust toolchain on this host?
decision_point.what_it_unblocks: a pinned build of the MIT-licensed core, its documented nuts-bolts run compared against the already-reproduced Python figures, and semantics-preserving expansion of out/out.json through the independent expander already written -- i.e. an H0/H2 library route whose licence is settled
decision_point.cost: $0 in licence; rustup and the MSVC-target toolchain are free and open
decision_point.footprint_NOT_MEASURED: a rustup toolchain plus a release build of ~22 dependencies is order-1 GiB of disk and minutes of CPU. That is an ESTIMATE from the dependency count and edition, not a measurement, and it is labelled so rather than quoted as a figure.
decision_point.also_needed: a C linker for the MSVC target. cc/link/cl presence is recorded above; MinGW is on PATH (cmake resolved through it earlier), so the gnu target may be the cheaper route. NOT verified.
decision_point.reversible: yes -- rustup self uninstall removes it
decision_point.alternative_if_declined: keep using the Python bindings under D-17's stricter reading: development-only, no export. Nothing currently running depends on lifting that.
